item: The launcher's record-lock takeover never moves a live lock (row 100)
summary: On the mkdir-lock path (no flock: macOS, and CI) two launchers could hold the record lock at once, and a trim then dropped an append (1 of 8 exit rows lost on CI). Two causes. (1) The takeover of a dead owner's lock moved the lock out and put a live one back. A taker now marks the lock with a reap mark born with its pid, reads the owner again under it and renames the lock away only if it still names the same dead owner. Dead takers' marks are cleared one clearer at a time, and a directory mark serves filesystems without hard links. (2) On systems whose mkdir is not exclusive (Ubuntu 26.04's uutils coreutils 0.10 reports success on a name another process just created), two launchers could both take the lock. The lock and the mark are now taken by an exclusive file create (noclobber, O_EXCL), never by mkdir alone. An eight-taker test fails on the old launcher, including with a non-exclusive mkdir, and its detector names both holders and the tools in use. The macOS timing test checks order, not a wall-clock budget. Residuals stated in the code: crashes inside a few instructions, long-lived pid reuse.
